To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of files at SLAC are used very few (less than five) times, that most of those files which are used sufficiently frequently to have their reference patterns studied are referenced in a non-Poisson, non-Markovian manner (a renewal process with a highly skewed interreference distribution), and that the majority of these files show declining rates of usage during their lifetimes.
the file reference patterns of most files can be modeled by a Poisson process with a skewed distribution of interreference times.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of algorithms for the automatic movement of data between on-line and mass storage devices.
the construction of algorithms to move files between on-line and off-line storage.
the development of file management techniques for large installations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are insufficient for the construction of a file migration algorithm based on file reference patterns.
the SLAC file reference patterns are not well described by the Bernoulli model.
the reference behavior of most active files is such that they are candidates for migration, and the algorithms developed and tested are capable of identifying and migrating such files.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a set of file reference statistics that may be useful for the construction of file migration algorithms.
the results of our analysis are not sufficiently conclusive to be used as the basis for the construction or application of file migration algorithms.

file migration algorithms should be based on file reference data and that the algorithms should be designed to migrate files with declining rates of reference and/or with skewed interreference intervals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
file reference patterns are highly variable.
the majority of active files are used infrequently and the majority of file references are to infrequently referenced files.
file migration algorithms should be based on file age, file usage, and the rate of file use.
